competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: Overnight tone stays dominated by triple-digit crude and Gulf shipping risk, with Brent near 118 and WTI above 104, gold holding near 3,899, and U.S. equities still elevated though the S&P print is older than the Dow and Nasdaq marks. The Fed's late-October hold and firm inflation rhetoric keep front-end U.S. rates anchored—SOFR 3.94 percent with the 10-year at 4.94 percent, about 35 basis points lower over the month—while earnings callers are again flagging cost pressure at the fastest pace since 2022. Hormuz headlines, including Iran claims, safe-passage diplomacy, and thin spare capacity, reinforce the oil bid; AI-related credit issuance stays active but uneven. The Bank of Japan held with underlying inflation at 2 percent yet weak spending expectations; the Bank of England is debating a higher-rate normal. New risk is open only in the United States this cycle. Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the euro area, and Japan cannot take fresh exposure because key consumer, activity, labor, and income releases could not be verified in time; existing positions may still be managed.

performance_reflections.what_happened_vs_expected: The fifth-to-twelfth slide with about 56743 against the book looked like a broken valuation book. Instead standing is back at fifth with about 59612 of net result and only 27 of giveback, while the live Australian dollar-Canada short kept working with Brent at 117.64. The dollar hit was the old United States-Canada pack, not a collapse of the five-year richness gap.
performance_reflections.no_new_lesson: A seven-place standing swing on about 57 thousand dollars versus a 100 million book is ordinary bounded variance around an already-booked pack loss and a still-working Australian dollar-Canada short; the prior process remains sound, so no new rule is required.

causal.original_belief: Falling from fifth to twelfth with about 57 thousand against the book meant the valuation process had failed and needed a style change.
causal.observed_reality: Standing is back at fifth with about 59 thousand of net result and only 27 of giveback; Australian dollar-Canada is 0.9813 versus 0.98787 entry, Brent is 117.64, and the prior 56 thousand realized hit was the old pack rather than a new thesis break.
causal.assumptions_right: Clustered desks can move several places on a small dollar result, and oil-supported Canadian terms of trade still argue the Australian dollar is rich versus the Canadian dollar on a five-year window.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Treating a clustered leaderboard print as proof that mean-reversion versus history had failed, and underweighting that the live cross had only just started to converge.
causal.causal_divergence: The standing shock was competition clustering around a small already-realized pack loss plus a lag before the live cross marked, not a collapse of the five-year richness gap or of the oil impulse.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: Covering or reversing the Australian dollar-Canada short on the twelfth-place print, with the cross still a five-year extreme and crude still three-digit, would have treated leaderboard noise as valuation information and would have missed the subsequent recovery.
